tagline: Who owns whom, who's designing where, and why 'quiet luxury' took over.
why: Luxury fashion is a giant business run by a few conglomerates, and its gossip is about creative directors swapping houses, prices rising, and what's 'in'. In Hong Kong luxury shopping is part of the city's identity, from Central's flagships to Harbour City. Knowing the big houses, their designers and the current trends makes it easy to talk style without being a fashionista.

essentials.title: A few groups own most brands
essentials.body: LVMH (Louis Vuitton, Dior, Celine, Loewe, Fendi, Tiffany), Kering (Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga), Richemont (Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, mostly jewellery and watches). Hermès and Chanel are independent and family-controlled.

essentials.title: Creative directors are the stars
essentials.body: Each house has a creative director who sets its look. When one moves, it's front-page news. 2025 saw a historic reshuffle at almost every major house.

essentials.title: The fashion calendar
essentials.body: Fashion weeks in New York, London, Milan and Paris twice a year show collections months ahead. Paris is the most important; haute couture is the hand-made top tier.

essentials.title: Logos vs quiet luxury
essentials.body: Fashion swings between loud logos (Gucci in the late 2010s) and 'quiet luxury', understated pieces without visible branding (Loro Piana, The Row, Brunello Cucinelli).

essentials.title: Prices keep rising
essentials.body: Luxury brands raised prices sharply after 2020. Some customers pushed back, and sales slowed in 2024-25, especially in China.

essentials.title: Streetwear and luxury merged
essentials.body: Supreme x Louis Vuitton (2017) and Virgil Abloh at Louis Vuitton made sneakers and hoodies part of luxury.

The designer who sets a brand's look.
Hand-made, made-to-measure fashion; legally protected term in France.

names.name: Bernard Arnault
names.what: Head of LVMH and among the world's richest people.

names.name: Chanel
names.what: Coco Chanel's house: the tweed jacket, the 2.55 bag, No. 5 perfume. Matthieu Blazy became creative director in 2025.

names.name: Louis Vuitton
names.what: The biggest luxury brand by sales. Pharrell Williams designs menswear.

names.name: Dior
names.what: LVMH's couture house. Jonathan Anderson took over all of Dior in 2025.

names.name: Gucci
names.what: Kering's biggest brand, struggling after its Alessandro Michele maximalist peak; Demna took over in 2025.

names.name: Hermès
names.what: The most exclusive and profitable house, famous for the Birkin and Kelly bags and silk scarves.

names.name: Prada / Miu Miu
names.what: Miuccia Prada's brands. Miu Miu has been the hottest brand of the mid-2020s. Prada bought Versace in 2025.

names.name: Loewe
names.what: Spanish leather house made cool by Jonathan Anderson; now led by Proenza Schouler's founders.

names.name: Bottega Veneta
names.what: Known for woven leather 'intrecciato' and no logos.

names.name: Saint Laurent
names.what: Sleek Parisian rock'n'roll style under Anthony Vaccarello.

names.name: Balenciaga
names.what: Made ugly-chic and oversized sneakers famous under Demna.

names.name: Uniqlo
names.what: Japanese basics giant, loved for value; its collabs with designers sell out.

names.name: Anna Wintour
names.what: Long-time Vogue editor, the most powerful figure in fashion media.

timeline.event: Hermès founded as a harness maker.
Coco Chanel opens her first shop.
LVMH formed by merging Louis Vuitton and Moët Hennessy.
Tom Ford revives Gucci with sexy minimalism.
Supreme x Louis Vuitton marks the streetwear takeover.
Virgil Abloh becomes LV menswear designer.
Quiet luxury trend after TV series Succession.
The great designer reshuffle at Chanel, Dior, Gucci, Balenciaga, Loewe and more.

now.headline: New designers everywhere
now.detail: Most big houses showed their first collections under new creative directors in 2025-26. Everyone has opinions on who got it right.

now.headline: Luxury slowdown
now.detail: After years of price hikes, sales slowed, especially in China, and brands are under pressure to justify prices.

now.headline: Miu Miu's moment
now.detail: Prada's younger sister brand has been one of the strongest performers.

now.headline: Dupes
now.detail: Cheap 'dupes' of luxury items are celebrated on TikTok, which annoys brands.

now.headline: K-pop ambassadors
now.detail: Stars from BLACKPINK, BTS and others front almost every major house in Asia.

local.headline: Luxury shopping hubs
local.detail: Central's Landmark and IFC, Pacific Place in Admiralty, Harbour City and Canton Road in Tsim Sha Tsui.

local.headline: Local department stores
local.detail: Lane Crawford and Joyce pioneered luxury retail in Hong Kong; I.T brings in edgier labels.

local.headline: Retail is changing
local.detail: Fewer mainland shoppers and Hong Kongers spending in Shenzhen have closed some luxury stores and lowered rents.

local.headline: Shanghai Tang
local.detail: The Hong Kong brand that modernised Chinese dress like the qipao.

debates.question: Is luxury still worth it?
debates.sides: Fans praise craftsmanship and design; critics say price rises outpaced quality.

debates.question: Quiet luxury or logos?
debates.sides: Understated is classy; logos are fun and recognisable.

debates.question: Is fast fashion OK?
debates.sides: Affordable style vs environmental waste and labour concerns.

debates.question: Do designer reshuffles help or hurt?
debates.sides: Fresh ideas vs losing a brand's identity.
